passages.title: Support for traveling believers makes truth practical while exclusion reveals a conflict over authority
passages.summary: The elder writes to Gaius, whom he loves in truth. He prays that Gaius will be healthy, as his soul prospers. Brothers have reported that Gaius walks in truth. Gaius has cared for traveling brothers, though they were strangers. They went out for the Name and took nothing from the Gentiles. Diotrephes loves to be first and refuses the elder’s messengers. He puts out of the assembly those who welcome them. Demetrius has a good report from everyone.

contextNote.title: Support for traveling believers makes truth practical while exclusion reveals a conflict over authority
contextNote.text: Verse 5 praises Gaius for what he does for brothers who are strangers. Verse 7 explains their need. They went out for the Name and accepted nothing from the Gentiles. Verse 8 gives the duty that follows: we “ought to receive such.” It also gives the host a title. Those who support them are fellow workers for the truth. Verses 9–10 show the opposite: Diotrephes refuses the brothers and stops others.
